title: Behaviour you can swap
description:
Inheritance fixes behaviour when the object is created. **Composition** lets you change it while the program runs: the object *has* a behaviour and can be handed a different one.

Write:

- an interface `IMovement` with `virtual std::string move() const = 0;`
- `Walk` (returns `"walks"`), `Fly` (returns `"flies"`), `Swim` (returns `"swims"`)
- a class `Robot`:
  - `Robot(std::string name, std::unique_ptr<IMovement> movement)`
  - `void setMovement(std::unique_ptr<IMovement> movement)`
  - `std::string act() const`: for example `"R2 walks"`. If the robot has no movement (a null pointer was given), it returns `"R2 stands still"`.

Notice there is no `FlyingRobot` or `SwimmingRobot` class, and no need for one.
